message.reasoning_content:
Analyze: kernel clamps rounded to [-255,255] then to int32 then adds z and clamps to [-128,127]. Contract: R can be large; clamp(rounded,-255,255) then +z clamped to [-128,127] — equivalent since R+z result clamping to [-128,127] means R beyond -255..255 never matters. Fine.

Potential bug: signed right shift in Triton — `>>` on int64 in Triton is arithmetic? Triton's >> on signed is arithmetic shift, yes. bias = 1<<(30+r) as int64, fine. product + bias in int64, fine.

Rounded >> then min/max. Also `tl.minimum(tl.maximum(bounded, -255), 255).to(tl.int32)` — bounded is int64. Fine.

Another concern: channel = index % CHANNELS with CHANNELS up to 257 — non-power-of-2 modulo is fine in Triton.

Also load with mask=active, other... fine. Contiguous views with nonzero storage offset: kernel loads ACC + index — pointer base is the view's data pointer, Triton handles that.

reference uses clamping only once at output — actually reference: rounded (no clamp) + z clamped. Kernel clamps rounded to ±255 then adds z clamp — since final clamp to [-128,127], any R outside [-255,255] gives... R=300, z=-128: kernel gives -128; reference gives 172→127. Different! But wait, can R exceed 255? P = a*m, |a| ≤ 2^31-1, m ≤ 2^31-1... P up to ~2^62, R = P >> (31+r), r≥0 so R up to 2^31-ish. Yes, R can be huge. Kernel: R clamped to 255, then +z, clamped to [-128,127] → 127 (if z ≥ -127... 255 + z: if z = -128, 127 → clamp 127. Always ≥127? 255 + (-128) = 127). So clamped R=255 always yields ≥127 → output 127. Reference: R + z clamped → also ≥ 127 whenever R+z ≥ 127. R ≥ 255? R ≥ 127 - z... If R huge, R+z ≥ huge - 128 ≥ 127. So both give saturation 127. Similarly negative: kernel clamp -255, +z (z≤127) → ≥ -128 → output -128... -255 + 127 = -128. Reference: R + z ≤ huge negative + 128 ≤ -128 → -128. So intermediate clamp to ±255 is harmless. Good.

So kernel looks correct. Let me just run a probe comparing to reference on random inputs plus adversarial (halfway cases, extreme values). Record a claim first.
